operator_io_quirks: All identifiers are backtick-quoted in DDL; generated SQL must double-quote them; names are mixed-case with underscores (no spaces).
Tiny DB: max 15 rows/table, 4-8 in parents; original_values sampling (k=min(5,len)) will often cover nearly the whole column.
Catalog_Contents_Additional_Attributes has NO primary key (pk=[]); sample_fresh_primary_keys must be a no-op there, and drop_unique_duplicates has no unique columns to act on.
Catalog_Contents has self-referential-looking columns parent_entry_id/previous_entry_id/next_entry_id but NO declared FK; they are plain Number columns, not self-FK.
Catalog_Contents_Additional_Attributes has a composite (catalog_entry_id, catalog_level_number) FK pair to two different parents; both are NOT NULL.
catalog_level_number values are non-contiguous (1,8,9) and reused as FK target by two child tables; parent PK is unique so FK fill is safe.
date_of_publication / date_of_latest_revision are DATETIME stored as TEXT 'YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS'; first element parses as int? no -> Date fuzzer with template %Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S.
capacity/length/height/width are VARCHAR but hold integer-like strings ('1','8'); String fuzzer will add str(i+1)/str(i-1) variants.
price_in_dollars/euros/pounds are DOUBLE (real storage); Number fuzzer with scale from no args -> default scale, float perturbation +-0.01/0.02.
attribute_data_type has distinct=1 ('Bool'); String fuzzer with 1 element -> p effectively 1, mostly returns the element.
product_stock_number format 'NN xx' (digits space letters); String fuzzer treats as generic text, no format preservation.
All null_rate=0.0; no NULLs in original, but TS may still emit NULLs for FK columns when parent empty (won't happen here since parents non-empty).
operator_ts_expectations: Date fuzzer on DATETIME columns: template from first parsable element '%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S', range from min/max of 4 distinct dates; fresh draws uniform in that range.
Number fuzzer on INTEGER PKs: full range [-10^scale,10^scale] with scale default; PK uniqueness enforced by sample_fresh_primary_keys, so PKs stay distinct but may be huge/negative.

Number fuzzer on DOUBLE prices: uniform in [-10^scale,10^scale] then +-0.01/0.02 perturbation; values may be negative or far from original 100-700 range -> implausible prices (FN risk on range predicates).
String fuzzer on names: random CHARSET strings with 0.5 contaminate; catalog_name/publisher become gibberish -> FN on LIKE/equality predicates.
String fuzzer on capacity/length/height/width: int-like strings get str(i+1)/str(i-1) added, so numeric comparisons may still work but random strings break them.

FK fill: Catalog_Structure.catalog_id drawn from Catalogs.catalog_id (8 values); Catalog_Contents.catalog_level_number from Catalog_Structure (3 values); Additional_Attributes draws from both parents.
Additional_Attributes has no PK, so no dedup; rows may repeat (catalog_entry_id, catalog_level_number, attribute_id) -> duplicates where original had distinct combos (FP risk on COUNT DISTINCT).
attribute_value only '0'/'1' (distinct=2); String fuzzer with 2 elements -> p=0.2 fresh random strings, mostly '0'/'1' -> plausible for Bool attribute.
attribute_data_type always 'Bool'; String fuzzer with 1 element returns it almost always -> stable, good for joins on attribute_data_type.
Small table sizes: choose_table_sizes level-0 = 1+30*u (1-31 rows), next level x4 capped 2500; parents stay tiny, children can be up to ~124 rows -> FK fan-out differs from original 15.
Self-referential columns (parent/previous/next_entry_id) are NOT FKs, so TS fills them with random Numbers, not valid entry ids -> FN on join-like predicates comparing them to catalog_entry_id.
Date columns have only 4 distinct values; TS Date fuzzer with p=0.2 returns element w.p. 0.2, else fresh uniform -> many distinct dates, breaking GROUP BY date / equality predicates (FN).
